title: Customers with Long Names
description:
Find customers whose full name is longer than **10 characters**.

**Table: customers** — `id`, `name`, `email`

Return `id`, `name`, and the name length aliased as `name_length`. Order by `name`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INT, name VARCHAR, email VARCHAR); INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1,'Alice','alice@example.com'),(2,'Bob Smith','bob@example.com'),(3,'Carol Johnson','carol@example.com'),(4,'Dave','dave@example.com'),(5,'Eve Williams','eve@example.com'),(6,'Frank Brown','frank@example.com'),(7,'Grace','grace@example.com'),(8,'Henry Martinez','henry@example.com');
solution_sql: SELECT id, name, LENGTH(name) AS name_length FROM customers WHERE LENGTH(name) > 10 ORDER BY name

test_cases.description: 4 customers have names longer than 10 characters: Carol Johnson(13), Eve Williams(12), Frank Brown(11), Henry Martinez(14)

hints: LENGTH(name) returns the number of characters in the string (including spaces).
You can use LENGTH() in both the SELECT list and the WHERE clause.
explanation: LENGTH() counts characters. 'Carol Johnson' = 13, 'Eve Williams' = 12, 'Frank Brown' = 11, 'Henry Martinez' = 14 — all exceed 10. 'Alice' = 5, 'Bob Smith' = 9, 'Dave' = 4, 'Grace' = 5 are all ≤ 10 and are excluded.
